Gold and silver came our way in the relays and that old war-horse Regis came up with a bronze medal but this time it was the field events that gave us our closest shots at individual gold. A medal at last for Mick Jones For Mick Jones Kuala Lumpur was a dream come true.

The Hammer competition at the European Champion Clubs Cup was held outside of the main stadium and with no cage! Who'd want to judge the event in those circumstances — and who'd want to be the photographer — we note that the man with the lens didn't get too close!

Mick Jones had a good competition and threw 72.55 for second place.

Mick Jones had been explaining to anyone who would listen that his training at Ockley Court Farm took place on a smooth concrete pad distanced some 75 metres from the nearest strawberry bed.
The hammer was first class with Mick Jones throwing a PB to beat Paul Head with both men over 73 metres. Matt Douglas clocked the same time as in Match 1 to win the 'A' 400H.

But this was after a dream start with Mick Jones and Dave Smith going head to head to win maximum points in the hammer. Dave's 70.84m was best to date indicating a gradual return to fitness but he was still to take second to Mick, although he did get the valuable scalp of Newham's Paul Head.
Mick Jones won the hammer in another PB.
The mighty Mick Jones. In far-off Kuala Lumpur a Commonwealth Games silver medal in the hammer throw was repayment for all those hours of practice in a farmer's field in Dorking, Surrey.

With Mick Jones on International duty, we press-ganged Dave Smith into action, even though he had been off since serious injury 6 months earlier.
Mick Jones and Dave Smith hoisted a winning double in a fine hammer event in which the Birchfield duo of Nickulin and Peacock were runners up.

Mick Jones won the 'A' hammer with a remarkable effort of 74.20 as he vainly chased the World Championship qualifying distance of 75.60. Disappointment for him but not for javelin winner Stuart Faben who won all bets as he slung the hammer more than 38m to get good points in the 'B' competition.

Our first end of week flutter happened when Mick Jones phoned in to say that he was enjoying himself with the family in the Isle of Wight. Pride of place must go to Phillips Idowu though - his 16.41 triple jump extended his Club Record by a further 6 cms. - and Mike Jones, who also set a new Belgrave best in the hammer.
Getting desperately close to the Olympic qualifying mark of 75.50, Mick Jones gave everything on his third throw only to lose his footing and end up lying across the circle having twisted his ankle.

Mike Jones retained his Hammer title after establishing an early lead but the big man from Sussex was still left searching for that elusive OQ standard that would see him included in the team.

Mick Jones was the right man to calm the nerves and despite having, on paper, a poorer performance than the Montreuil thrower he beat him by some distance and took the stadium record for good measure.
The start seemed straight forward enough with Mick Jones winning the hammer with a 74m plus effort - some 5.5m ahead of second place Paul Head.

Our usual good start looked decidedly iffy as Mick Jones slipped around the waterlogged hammer circle. Going into the last round in an unusual second spot only Mick seemed confident that he could retain his 3 year unbeaten record.
Mick Jones retained his unbeaten record in the hammer, while Stuart Faben gained his first ever win in the 'A' javelin. Wesley Smith gained silver in the 'B' javelin improving yet again to 57.29m.
In the hammer Mick Jones' 'A' win and Phil Spivey's 'B' silver were matched by a second and a win. We pulled ahead slightly in the discus with Lee again pipping Kevin Brown.

Our start was as usual excellent with a lack lustre win from Mick Jones in the hammer. Mick was still recovering from four week absence due to injury and was spending his time going from meet to meet in search of the big one.

A dozen medallists at the AAA Championships included two winners - Mick Jones in the hammer and Phillips Idowu in triple jump. Vernicha James became our first global champion since John Regis when she won the World Junior 200 metre Championship in Jamaica.

And performances don't come any more meritorious than those set by the man who has aptly been described as one of the most popular men in our sport - hammer man Mick Jones.

In the men's throws Mick Jones and Greg Beard performed superbly with Greg's 16.17m in the shot heralding a return to form in a big way. Shot putter Eva Massey's 15.71m was not far short of her season's best.

Mick Jones, only just back from adventures in Canada, was in the land of nod when he should have been reporting for the hammer. Fortunately Kevin Brown stepped in but his single point was lost in the discus where injury relegated him to fourth spot.

The hammer, later in the programme than usual, saw John Osazuwa make a welcome return ensuring he and Mick Jones walked off with near maximum points, while on the track we gained our only maximum points (and in the steeplechase too) with Martin Dent breaking the stadium record and Kevin Nash recordi…

Mick Jones moved house in the week and it showed; but he came, and his support was greatly appreciated. A special mention for John Osazuwa who gained good points in the B hammer with a season’s best effort of 59.22m, and long jumper Darragh O’Farrell who produced a 53.33m effort in the javelin.

Only Mick Jones lined up for the hammer and once again finished second best to Andy Frost of WGEL. Points were also down in the pole vault after Cameron Johnson had withdrawn the night before due to injury.

William Sharman claimed top spot on his own this year as only he, Mick Jones and new member Adrian Phillips made all four matches. There will be some serious revisions to the all time points scores table as many of our big points scorers continued to rack up impressive contributions to the team’s efforts.

Australian Marty Dent had a cracking run in the 3000 metres Steeplechase - first man home after the Kenyan clean sweep – and in his fifth Commonwealth Games Mick Jones went over 70 metres in the hammer to place 5th.

Gloom had already descended on the Belgrave supporters after the first few events which suffered from below par performances: a “no height” in the pole vault and a “no distance” in the hammer, while Commonwealth games returnees, Mick Jones and Matt Douglas, suffered a drop in performance and paid the price.

Then to the hammer with a slimmed down Mick Jones gaining third in the A closely followed by John Osazuwa who won the B. Back on the track, William Sharman again eased to victory in the A 110 hurdles clocking a fine 13.85 secs into a big headwind.
Mick Jones then had a good series in the hammer and was ably supported by event debutant Mark Allen and still we were on our predicted points target as attention switched to the track.
